items.title: Section: Treasuring Non-Buddhist Doctrine Instead of Treating It as Bitter Medicine

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，越菩薩法，於異道論及諸外論研求善巧，深心寶翫、愛樂、味著，非如辛藥而習近之，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who overstep the proper bounds of bodhisattva practice, pursuing skill in rival and non-Buddhist treatises with a mind that genuinely treasures, delights in, and grows attached to them — approaching them not as one approaches a necessary but bitter medicine, but as something to be savoured for its own sake — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation.

items.title: Section: Slandering the Profound Teaching Out of Simple Incomprehension

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，聞菩薩藏，於甚深處最勝甚深真實法義、諸佛菩薩難思神力，不生信解，憎背毀謗：不能引義、不能引法，非如來說，不能利益安樂有情。是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。如是毀謗，或由自內非理作意，或隨順他而作是說。若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，若聞甚深最甚深處，心不信解，菩薩爾時應強信受，應無諂曲，應如是學：我為非善，盲無慧目，於如來眼隨所宣說，於諸如來密意語言而生誹謗。菩薩如是自處無知，仰推如來，於諸佛法無不現知等隨觀見。如是正行，無所違犯。雖無信解，然不誹謗。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, hearing the bodhisattva canon's most profound and truest teachings, and the buddhas' and bodhisattvas' inconceivable spiritual powers, cannot generate faith and understanding, and respond with hostility and slander — declaring that such teaching cannot yield genuine value, cannot yield the true dharma, is not what the Tathāgata actually taught, and cannot benefit or bring ease to any being — commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. Such slander arises either from one's own unwise reflection, or simply from repeating what others have said. ... Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, hearing the most profound teachings, find no faith or understanding arising in their own minds, should at that very moment compel themselves to accept the teaching with genuine trust, free of any pretence, training themselves to think: "This lack is my own failing — I am like one blind, lacking the eye of wisdom; towards what the Tathāgata's own eye has proclaimed, and towards the Tathāgata's own hidden intent within these words, I would otherwise give rise to slander." Positioning themselves honestly as simply not yet knowing, and looking up to the Tathāgata instead, whose wisdom leaves nothing among all things whatsoever unseen and fully realised — conducting oneself rightly in this way incurs no violation at all. Though understanding has not yet arisen, no slander follows from it.

items.title: Section: Praising Oneself and Disparaging Others Out of Jealousy for Recognition

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於他人所有染愛心、有瞋恚心，自讚毀他，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。無違犯者，若為摧伏諸惡外道；若為住持如來聖教；若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；或欲令其未淨信者發生淨信，已淨信者倍復增長。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, towards what belongs to another, harbour a craving, attached mind, and a mind of hostile resentment, and praise themselves while disparaging the other person, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. ... There is no violation when done to subdue genuinely harmful non-Buddhist opponents; to uphold and preserve the Tathāgata's own sacred teaching; as a skilful means to guide and subdue a particular being, as described more fully earlier; or to give rise to genuine faith in someone not yet faithful, or to deepen the faith of someone already faithful.

items.title: Section: Refusing Out of Pride to Attend a Dharma Talk — and the Eight Marks of Genuinely Skilful Teaching

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，聞說正法論議決擇，憍慢所制，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，而不往聽，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若為嬾惰懈怠所蔽，而不往聽，非染違犯。無違犯者，若不覺知；若有疾病；若無氣力；若知倒說；若為護彼說法者心；若正了知彼所說義，是數所聞、所持、所了；若已多聞，具足聞持，其聞積集；若欲無間於境住心，若勤引發菩薩勝定；若自了知上品愚鈍，其慧鈍濁，於所聞法難受難持，難於所緣攝心令定；不往聽者，皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, hearing that the true dharma is being taught, discussed, or carefully analysed nearby, are gripped by arrogance, resentment, or hostility and so do not go to listen — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If it is mere laziness or indolence that keeps them away, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation whatsoever: for one who simply does not know a talk is happening; who is genuinely ill; who lacks the physical strength; who knows the teaching being given is actually mistaken; who stays away to protect the speaker's state of mind; who already correctly understands the very material being discussed, having heard, retained, and mastered it many times before; who is already deeply learned, having fully retained everything heard, with that learning thoroughly consolidated; who wishes, without interruption, to keep the mind settled on a meditation object; who is diligently working to cultivate a bodhisattva's own superior concentration; or who honestly recognises their own dull and clouded intelligence, finding such teaching genuinely too difficult to receive, retain, or settle the mind upon.

items.title: Section: Disrespecting the Dharma Teacher — All Thirty-Two Precepts of Gathering Wholesome Dharmas Complete

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於說法師故思輕毀，不深恭敬，嗤笑調弄，但依於文不依於義，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who deliberately belittle and disrespect a dharma teacher, withhold proper reverence, mock and ridicule them, and attend only to the elegance of the phrasing rather than to the correctness of the meaning — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation.

items.title: Section: The Benefiting-Beings Cluster Opens — Refusing to Lend a Helping Hand

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於諸有情所應作事，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，不為助伴。謂於能辦所應作事，或於道路若往若來，或於正說事業加行，或於掌護所有財寶，或於和好乖離諍訟，或於吉會，或於福業，不為助伴，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若為嬾惰懈怠所蔽，不為助伴，非染違犯。無違犯者，若有疹疾；若無氣力；若了知彼自能成辦；若知求者自有依怙；若知所作能引非義、能引非法；若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；若先許餘為作助伴；若轉請他有力者助；若於善品正勤修習，不欲暫廢；若性愚鈍，於所聞法難受難持，如前廣說；若為將護多有情意；若護僧制；不為助伴，皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, gripped by resentment or hostility, refuse to lend a hand with a being's worthwhile undertaking — travelling with them on the road, assisting a dharma-teaching effort, guarding their entrusted wealth, mediating a rift towards reconciliation, accompanying them to an auspicious gathering, or joining an act of merit-making — commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness or indolence keeps them from lending a hand, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation whatsoever: for one who is ill; who lacks the physical strength; who knows the other can manage the task unaided; who knows the one requesting help already has other support; who knows the undertaking would actually lead towards what is meaningless or unwholesome; who withholds help purely as a skilful means to guide the other, as described more fully earlier; who has already promised to help someone else; who redirects the request to someone else more capable; who is diligently absorbed in wholesome practice and does not wish to interrupt it even briefly; who honestly knows their own dullness makes them unable to receive or retain what is asked of them, as described more fully earlier; who withholds help purely to protect the feelings of the larger community; or who withholds help specifically to uphold a rule the monastic community has properly established.

items.title: Section: Refusing to Visit and Attend to the Seriously Ill — and On Speaking Gently to the Dying

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，見諸有情遭重疾病，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，不往供事，是名有犯，有所違越。是染違犯。若為嬾惰懈怠所蔽，不往供事，非染違犯。無違犯者，若自有病；若無氣力；若轉請他有力隨順令往供事；若知病者有依有怙；若知病者自有勢力，能自供事；若了知彼長病所觸，堪自支持；若為勤修廣大無上殊勝善品；若欲護持所修善品，令無間缺；若自了知上品愚鈍，其慧鈍濁，於所聞法難受難持，難於所緣攝心令定；若先許餘為作供事。如於病者，於有苦者為作助伴，欲除其苦，當知亦爾。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who see beings suffering serious illness, and who, gripped by resentment or hostility, refuse to go and attend to them, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness or indolence keeps them away, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation: for one who is themselves ill; who lacks the physical strength; who redirects a capable other person to go instead; who knows the sick person already has proper support; who knows the sick person can manage on their own; who knows the person is simply managing a long-term chronic condition well enough already; who is diligently cultivating vast, unsurpassed, supremely wholesome practice; who does not wish to interrupt an ongoing practice even briefly; who honestly recognises their own dull and clouded intelligence makes such visits difficult to conduct wisely; or who has already promised to attend someone else. Exactly as with the physically ill, so too should attending and seeking to relieve anyone in genuine distress be understood.

blocks.text: The last wisdom precepts, then those concerning benefiting beings.

Studying other schools is permitted, but "with a mind that treasures them, delighting in them as if nectar" is an offence. Venerable Miào Jìng: treat them like bitter medicine, which tastes bad but helps.

Hearing "the bodhisattva canon's most profound teachings" and slandering them for not understanding is an offence. Instead one should say: "I am unskilled, blind in wisdom; the Buddha's teaching is beyond me." Master Cháng Bǎi: "profound" is the Dharma taught; "most profound", the Dharma realised.
Praising oneself and disparaging others out of craving and jealousy is an offence. Venerable Miào Jìng: jealousy is being unable to bear others' glory.
Not going to hear the Dharma "out of arrogance or resentment": tainted; from laziness, untainted. Master Cháng Bǎi: one exception is when one's presence would put the speaker under pressure.
Belittling a Dharma teacher, "attending only to the elegance of the phrasing rather than the meaning": always tainted, with no exceptions (Master Cháng Bǎi).

Refusing out of resentment to help with "a being's worthwhile undertaking": travelling, work, guarding property, reconciling quarrels. Exceptions: when they can manage alone, or the task would lead to harm.
Refusing to visit the seriously ill out of resentment. Master Cháng Bǎi: don't walk in and tell a dying patient "Let go!" at once; it can make things worse. Speak gently.

quiz.q: Treasuring, delighting in, and savouring outside doctrine "rather than approaching it like bitter medicine" is a tainted violation. How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe these?
options: first treasuring, then delighting, then savouring; bitter medicine tastes bad but one takes it because one needs it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: first treasuring, then delighting, then savouring. Bitter medicine tastes bad, but because one needs it one takes it reluctantly. Master Cháng Bǎi: study taken as bitter medicine is for countering or converting outsiders.

quiz.q: When a bodhisattva cannot believe a profound teaching, how does the treatise say to think?
options: accept it by effort, thinking "I am unskilled, blind without wisdom's eye," taking ignorance upon oneself and deferring to the Tathāgata — not believing yet, but not slandering
declare it not the Buddha's word
quiz.why: The bodhisattva "should accept it by effort, without pretence, and train thus: I am unskilled, blind without the eye of wisdom… though lacking faith and understanding, one does not slander." Venerable Miào Jìng: pretence is saying you believe while not believing inside.

quiz.q: "The profound and the most supremely profound." How do the two lectures distinguish them?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the profound is the taught dharma, the most profound is the realised dharma; Miào Jìng: the profound is dharma (wording), the most profound is meaning
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "the profound" is the dharma as taught; "the most profound" is the dharma as realised. Venerable Miào Jìng: "the profound" is the dharma, "the most profound" is its meaning — one dharma, one meaning.

quiz.q: "With craving and hostility towards what belongs to another, praising oneself and disparaging the other" — what affliction do the lectures identify behind it?
options: jealousy — being unable to bear another's success
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: being unable to bear others' glory is called jealousy. Master Cháng Bǎi: the affliction of not tolerating others' success appears. Miào Jìng adds that praising the dharma and rebuking outsiders is not a violation.

quiz.q: If one fails to attend a dharma talk out of mere laziness, how does the treatise judge it?
quiz.why: Out of arrogance or resentment it is tainted; "if it is mere laziness or indolence that keeps them away," it is untainted. Master Cháng Bǎi on "not knowing about it": no knowledge, no fault.

quiz.q: Besides belittling and mocking the dharma teacher, what wrong listening attitude does the treatise name?
options: attending to the wording rather than the meaning
quiz.why: Belittling the teacher, mocking them, and "attend[ing] only to the elegance of the phrasing rather than to the correctness of the meaning" is a tainted violation. Master Cháng Bǎi: deciding whether to listen by how pleasant it sounds, not by whether the principles are right.

quiz.q: On visiting the seriously ill, what does Master Cháng Bǎi advise?
options: first ask about how they feel inside; saying "let go!" right away can make things worse
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: going in and immediately telling the patient "Let go!" can actually make the illness worse; in caring for the sick, first ask about how they feel inside.
